I'm not too great either, MG1 and rising at the moment. Here's an assortment of hopefully useful information:

Deathmatch: The built in valve deathmatch isn't great. Weapons restricted by team, too-long respawn invulnerability, and TDM only. So it's better to search for DM servers in the community server browser, and play a mix of classic FFA, TDM on aim maps, HS-only FFA, and pistol only FFA.

Surf and KZ maps Search the community servers for surf and KZ maps, and learn to surf and bhop. Bhopping doesn't work well in matchmaking, but learning air control is still helpful in many situations. Also I feel that surfing can help train very precise and methodical muscle memory, which might be helpful in aiming.

Mouse: Set your sensitivity as low as you can tolerate, and maybe a bit lower after that, and get a bigger mousepad. It will make your snap aiming more consistent, since you will have a physically larger margin of error when you move your mouse. I have 800dpi and 1.35sens, which is on the high side of what pro players use (often pros use 400dpi and 1.5-2.5 sens).

Aspect ratio: You might find some benefit in setting your game to a 4:3 resolution, stretched to fit your 16:9 monitor (assuming that's what you have). You lose some peripheral vision, but everything looks a little "zoomed in".

Workshop maps: There are tons of aim, grenade, and jump training maps on the workshop. training_aim_csgo2_dark is a great aim training map, with features for practicing snap aiming, tracking, bursting, and reaction time. Recoil Master lets you practice the unique burst patterns of the various ARs, SMGs, and LMGs. Crashz is a workshop creator who has made several useful maps, including a crosshair generator map, and smoke practice maps for dust 2 and cache.

Launch options: You can set a variety of launch options that get the game to open faster and reliably have some useful settings enabled. These are my game launch options: -novid -tickrate 128 -refresh 75 -window -w 1280 -h 1025 -noborder +exec autoexec.cfg . In order these settings disable the valve logo opening video, set the game tick and refresh rates, open the game in a 1280x1025 borderless window, and run a config file with some more potentially useful settings (like viewmodel or crosshair settings).

LEM here. Not the best but I've put a lot of hours in.

Biggest thing by far for me is working on aim and spray control. I usually do 10-20 minutes in DM with the m4s, deagle or ak ONLY going for headshots. Also, learn to control your shots. Fire short 1-3 shot bursts while in prActice and resist the urge to spray.

My gf wanted to try the game, so I told her to aim for the head and only fire one or two shots at a time. She went 10/30 her first DM match, and she has NEVER played any shooter, or ANY PC game. A good foundation will take you far.

Next step after basics is to learn how to use grenades. Good timing on your smokes for movement (something I didn't really try until about 300hrs in) is a huge advantage. Also using flash bangs and he grenades liberally can really pay off, especially against people who don't know how to use them themselves.

Good luck and have fun! If you ever want to mess around and ask for some tips, I'm happy to give you my steam id.

Go to the csgo workshop. Find recoil master and aim training for practice. Those will help with your shooting. Make sure you play with headphones and pay attention to footstep noises. Learning to use sound to your advantage is important. Lastly, pick a few competitive maps you want to play and learn the callouts. Good luck and have fun!
